books.title: Orchard Almanac
books.text:
The Orchard Almanac, kept by the hill growers.

Apples ripen from the tallest branch down, so pick the high fruit first and leave the windfalls for the pigs. The sweet red variety keeps through winter in a cool cellar if each fruit is wrapped in dry straw; the green kind does not keep and should be eaten or pressed within the week.

Prune in the dead of winter, never in the wet of spring. Cut to an outward bud, remove any limb that crosses another, and burn the clippings well away from the trees. A healthy orchard is thinned a little every year rather than a great deal every few.
